record.context_brief: Ricci-flow proof of the Soul theorem
record.original_question: Can one prove the real or complex Soul theorem by Ricci flow, rather than by the original Cheeger-Gromoll analysis via the Busemann function and Toponogov's theorem?

evidence.quote: Question 4.13. Can we prove the real or complex version of the Soul theorem by the Ricci flow ? Note that Cheeger-Gromoll proved the Soul theorem by analyzing the Busemann function, and their argument envoked the Toponogov theorem. Maybe the Ricci flow can give a more direct proof.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the Soul theorem of Cheeger–Gromoll: every complete, connected, noncompact Riemannian manifold (M, g) of nonnegative sectional curvature admits a closed, totally convex, totally geodesic embedded submanifold S (a "soul"), and M is diffeomorphic to the total space of the normal bundle of S in M. There is also a complex analogue for complete Kähler manifolds of nonnegative holomorphic bisectional (or sectional) curvature, in which the soul is a complex submanifold and M is biholomorphic to a holomorphic vector bundle over it.

The original proof of Cheeger–Gromoll proceeds by analyzing the Busemann function associated with rays in M and invokes Toponogov's triangle comparison theorem.

Problem. Give a proof of the Soul theorem — in either its real Riemannian form or its complex Kähler form — that uses the Ricci flow
   ∂g(t)/∂t = −2 Ric(g(t)),   g(0) = g,
as its main tool, in place of the Busemann function / Toponogov comparison argument of Cheeger–Gromoll. That is, construct a Ricci-flow-based argument that produces the soul S ⊂ M and establishes that M is diffeomorphic (respectively biholomorphic) to the normal bundle of S.
artifact.status_search_result: The classical Soul theorem (Cheeger–Gromoll 1972) and the Soul conjecture (Perelman 1994) have well-known proofs based on Busemann functions, Toponogov comparison, and convexity arguments. A web search did not surface a published Ricci-flow proof of the real or complex Soul theorem that replaces the Cheeger–Gromoll method; the question of finding such a Ricci-flow-based proof appears not to have been resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Soul theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Cheeger and Gromoll proved the theorem in 1972 ... The related soul conjecture ... was proved twenty years later by Grigori Perelman.
status_evidence.claim: Standard proofs of the Soul theorem and Soul conjecture use Busemann/convexity methods rather than Ricci flow.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the soul conjecture of Cheeger and Gromoll - Perelman
status_evidence.snippet: Perelman's concise proof of the Soul conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Perelman's proof of the Soul conjecture does not employ Ricci flow as its main mechanism.
